result: C. elegans forms a memory of familiar food that lasts at least 7 hours and selectively increases feeding on familiar bacteria. This behavioral plasticity depends on the duration of exposure but not on timing of exposure or nutritional status.

result: Recognition of familiar food specifically activates ADF chemosensory neurons, which release more serotonin in response to familiar bacteria than novel bacteria.

result: Serotonin from ADF acts humorally to directly activate SER-7 receptors in MC motor neurons, which then activate cholinergic transmission to pharyngeal muscles to increase feeding.

result: Serotonin controls feeding through multiple receptors: positively via SER-7 and negatively via SER-4 and MOD-1, with both pathways more active on familiar food.
